summary: Sid Meier's foundational 4X strategy franchise, covering the seven mainline Civilization games, multiplayer/remake variants, Call to Power branch, Revolution spin-offs, Beyond Earth, and social/mobile entries.

entries.title: Sid Meier's Civilization

emulation.notes: Use DOSBox or Windows compatibility tooling.

primary.why: The original Civilization was developed for PC and later ported widely; PC remains the most faithful and configurable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the DOS/Windows PC release with DOSBox/compatibility tooling; use console/computer ports only for comparison.

secondary.why: They are adaptations rather than the best main route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster; CivNet covers multiplayer separately.

entries.title: Sid Meier's CivNet

emulation.notes: Use period Windows compatibility/VM for LAN/hotseat testing.

primary.why: CivNet is the multiplayer-focused Windows remake/update of the original Civilization.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Windows 3.1/95 compatibility tooling or a VM if multiplayer/Simultaneous turns need preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Multiplayer remake/update of Civilization, not a sequel.

entries.title: Civilization II
entries.definitive_edition: Civilization II Multiplayer Gold/complete PC route

emulation.notes: Use compatibility tooling for legacy Windows builds.

primary.version: Civilization II Multiplayer Gold Edition / Complete route
primary.why: Civilization II is Windows-first, and the later bundled/complete PC routes include multiplayer and expansion content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows complete/multiplayer route with compatibility fixes; use PlayStation only for port comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: Test of Time is a separate remake/expanded entry.

entries.title: Civilization II: Test of Time

emulation.notes: Use compatibility tooling for legacy Windows builds.

primary.why: Test of Time is a Windows-only remake/expanded Civilization II variant with sci-fi and fantasy campaigns.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Windows with compatibility fixes after Civilization II if archiving the variant campaigns.

entries.remaster_caveats: Separate expanded/remake branch of Civilization II.

entries.title: Civilization: Call to Power

primary.why: Call to Power is the Activision Civilization branch; Windows is the lead and best-supported route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release or a compatible digital re-release; use Linux/Mac/BeOS only for port preservation.

secondary.why: The content is not preferred over Windows, but the platform release is historically unusual.

entries.remaster_caveats: Activision branch rather than Firaxis mainline.

entries.title: Call to Power II
entries.definitive_edition: Windows release with community patch/Apolyton Edition where appropriate

primary.why: Call to Power II is Windows-only and later received source-code/community patch support, making the modern Windows community-patched route the best preservation option.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with current community patch/Apolyton Edition where desired.

entries.remaster_caveats: Title omits Civilization because the name license was lost.

primary.why: Civilization III Complete bundles the base game with Play the World and Conquests, making Windows the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Civilization III Complete on Windows with compatibility fixes.

entries.title: Civilization IV
entries.definitive_edition: Civilization IV: The Complete Edition on Windows

primary.why: The Complete Edition bundles Civilization IV with Warlords, Beyond the Sword, and Colonization, making Windows the most complete/flexible route.
primary.how_to_play: Play The Complete Edition on Windows; use Colonization as a separate entry if treating it as a standalone remake.

entries.remaster_caveats: Complete Edition includes expansions; Colonization is tracked separately.

entries.title: Civilization IV: Colonization

primary.why: Colonization is a standalone remake using the Civilization IV engine and is best on Windows.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release, either standalone or through Civilization IV Complete.

entries.remaster_caveats: Remake of Sid Meier's Colonization, not a mainline Civilization IV expansion.

primary.why: Civilization Revolution is a console/handheld spin-off; Xbox 360 is a strong HD route while DS/mobile versions are lower-fidelity adaptations.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware/backward compatibility where available; use DS/iOS/Windows Phone only for platform comparison.

secondary.what_to_play: Sample only for handheld version preservation.
secondary.why: It is a distinct lower-fidelity portable route.

entries.title: Civilization V
entries.definitive_edition: Civilization V: Complete Edition on Windows

primary.why: The Complete Edition bundles Gods & Kings, Brave New World, and DLC; Windows is the most complete and moddable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Civilization V Complete on Windows with current Steam/GOG-compatible setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: Complete Edition includes major expansions and DLC.

primary.why: Civilization World was a Facebook MMO/social strategy game and was shut down in 2013, so it is a preservation/shutdown entry.
primary.how_to_play: No official live route remains; archive only with verified client/server/web preservation.

entries.title: Civilization Revolution 2
entries.definitive_edition: Civilization Revolution 2 Plus on PlayStation Vita

emulation.notes: Verify compatibility; Vita hardware is safest.

primary.why: The Vita Plus release adds exclusive scenarios, units, and leaders compared with the mobile original, making it the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Civilization Revolution 2 Plus on Vita for the exclusive content; Android/iOS are useful for mobile preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Vita Plus adds content compared with mobile versions.

entries.title: Civilization: Beyond Earth
entries.definitive_edition: Beyond Earth with Rising Tide on Windows

primary.why: Beyond Earth is PC-first, and the Rising Tide expansion is the most complete route for its systems/content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows release with Rising Tide installed; use Mac/Linux only as equivalent native routes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Spiritual successor to Alpha Centauri, not mainline Civilization VII/V sequel.

primary.why: Rising Tide is the major Beyond Earth expansion and is best played on Windows with the base game.
primary.how_to_play: Install Rising Tide on the Windows version of Beyond Earth.

primary.version: Civilization VI Anthology / complete DLC route
primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity/moddable route and the Anthology/complete DLC package covers Rise and Fall, Gathering Storm, and additional content.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Anthology/current complete package; use console/mobile ports only for portability.

entries.title: Civilization VII
entries.definitive_edition: Current Windows complete/Founders or Settler package

primary.why: Civilization VII is the latest mainline entry; Windows is the highest-fidelity and most configurable route, with the broadest long-term mod/support expectation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the current Windows build via Steam/Epic; document patch version, DLC collection, and 2K account-linked bonuses.

entries.remaster_caveats: Record patch/DLC/account-bonus state; Apple Arcade edition is a separate subscription route.

entries.title: Sid Meier's Colonization
entries.definitive_edition: Classic DOS Colonization through DOSBox/current PC storefront, with remakes documented separately

emulation.notes: Use DOSBox/current PC package for primary; emulate Amiga/Mac only for version comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original DOS release on period hardware or documented DOSBox setup

primary.version: Classic Colonization DOS release from current PC storefront
primary.why: This is the original 1994 Colonization, distinct from Civilization IV: Colonization. The current GOG/Steam-style DOSBox PC route is the practical archive path, while Amiga/Mac/Windows 3.1 ports and FreeCol/Civ IV remake should be documented separately.
primary.how_to_play: Use the classic DOS release through DOSBox or a current storefront package. Record source, DOSBox version, sound device, difficulty, nation, map, independence victory state, save/version, and whether Amiga/Mac/Windows 3.1, FreeCol, or Civilization IV: Colonization were compared.

secondary.why: DOS/current PC is the practical main route.

secondary.exclusive_content: Open-source remake and official Civ IV-engine remake
secondary.why: They are remakes/reimplementations, not the original game route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Do not merge this entry with Civilization IV: Colonization; it is the 1994 original.
